headline_recommendation.selected_option: Self-apply Part B of PROP-077 per operator's Q_OP_1=YES decision in DIRECTIVE-20260603-003. Edit monitor/prompts/structure-integrity.md to add a clone-source-of-truth PROLOGUE to Section 7h (Mech-A-Bypass False-Closure Audit, the section whose self-test caused the 2026-06-03T01:30:38Z revert via 3a709c71) AND Section 7a.5 (ISS ID-Collision Audit, the only other integrity section that reads open-issues.json + writes a 'file a new ISS' instruction) AND a one-line note in the Context section establishing the clone-as-source-of-truth principle for monitor/decisions/* + monitor/analyst/* writes. Additionally, per Q_OP_4 narrowed scope (decider only), grep decider.md + reference/decider-*.md for explicit clone-source-of-truth language; if implicit, add one line near Step 0 / clone-refresh discipline.
headline_recommendation.rationale_one_paragraph: PROP-077's H5 root cause is structurally addressed only by Part B — the workspace-sync recent-commit guard (Part A, shipped) is defense-in-depth that wouldn't have prevented the 2026-06-03 incident because integrity bypassed workspace-sync entirely. The H5 mechanism: integrity's Haiku agent runs Section 7h's self-test using a cwd-relative read of monitor/decisions/open-issues.json which resolves to the stale FUSE copy (cross-session staleness from decider's ca68cb5d commit at 01:23:55Z), appends ISS-2519 in memory, writes the modified blob to its fresh clone (overwriting the clone's already-fresh content), and pushes. The fix is to mandate that integrity (and every writer for these files) reads AND writes ONLY from its fresh clone. Decider's discipline is already strong (Step 0 refreshes clean clone; reads from CLEAN_CLONE explicitly in many code paths; PROP-076 Mech-A audit added a pre-push lint gate) but the principle isn't stated as a single explicit rule — adding one line near Step 0 closes the discoverability gap without restructuring. analyst / analyst-baby / tinker prompts are held back per Q_OP_4: revisit if recurrence shows up there.

(2) Section 7a.5 gains a PROLOGUE block (~6 LOC). (3) Section 7h gains a PROLOGUE block (~8 LOC). (4) monitor/prompts/decider.md gains a 1-line note near Step 0 (if grep reveals the rule is implicit).

decider_audit_findings.verdict: (b) Rule is IMPLICIT but not explicitly stated as a single principle. Discipline is strong (every code path uses ${CLEAN_CLONE} or 'the clone'), but a Haiku agent re-reading the prompt looking for first-principles guidance on 'where do I read open-issues.json from?' won't find a one-shot answer. Surgical fix: add one line near Step 0 (decider.md ~line 37) elevating the implicit discipline to an explicit principle. ZERO contradictions found — there is no place where decider prompts tell the agent to read these files from FUSE.

regression_check.before: structure-integrity.md Sections 7a.5 and 7h have implicit cwd-relative reads of monitor/decisions/*. Integrity Haiku agent's default behavior reads from FUSE when cwd is the FUSE workspace or its own session-relative path. The 2026-06-03T01:30Z incident is the canonical failure shape.
regression_check.after: Sections 7a.5 and 7h explicitly mandate clone-relative paths. Integrity must be invoked from inside its fresh clone (already true for the build-reproducibility section per existing /tmp/dome-integrity-clone wording, but not previously enforced for open-issues.json reads/writes). The PROLOGUE in each section makes the read+write path unambiguous.

regression_check.edge_case_first_run_integrity_no_clone: If integrity's first-ever run has no pre-existing clone, its session is expected to fall through to /tmp/dome-integrity-clone for Section 9 (Build Reproducibility). If a future regression strips that setup, this PROLOGUE makes the failure mode loud (no clone → no open-issues.json read source → audit fails fast).

could_part_b_be_a_lighter_implementation.objection: A single one-line note in the intro might suffice; do we really need PROLOGUEs in BOTH Section 7h AND Section 7a.5?
could_part_b_be_a_lighter_implementation.response: Haiku-model integrity reads its own prompt in chunks. A Context-level rule placed 540+ lines before Section 7h's self-test won't reliably ground the agent at the moment of the write. The local PROLOGUE at the audit-write site is what closes the gap — same pattern proven by PROP-077 Part A (the recent-commit guard goes inside smart_copy, not in workspace-sync.md's intro). Section 7a.5 gets the same treatment because it's the next-most-likely surface for a similar bug; the directive explicitly named both sections.

why_decider_audit_at_all_if_no_evidence_.objection: Decider's clone discipline is strong; why add a one-liner?
why_decider_audit_at_all_if_no_evidence_.response: Operator's Q_OP_4 narrowed scope to decider precisely because decider is the highest-prolific writer in this class. The discipline is implicit; the PROP-076 Mech-A bypass case shows that implicit-discipline-without-explicit-statement leaks under model-variation. Adding one line costs ~0 prompt budget (a 1-line statement in a 1207-line file) and elevates the rule to first-class. Cheap insurance.

could_the_rule_extend_to_curmudgeon_or_o.objection: Curmudgeon, analyst, social, etc. all read/write monitor/decisions/* and monitor/analyst/*. Why only integrity and decider?
could_the_rule_extend_to_curmudgeon_or_o.response: Directive non-goals #6: 'Do NOT auto-extend the clone-source-of-truth rule to monitor/curmudgeon/* or monitor/tinker/* in this run — those have different ownership patterns and the rule may not apply uniformly. Stay scoped to monitor/decisions/* + monitor/analyst/*.' Operator-set scope. Curmudgeon's discipline is also strong (clone-fresh-each-run; reads its priority-queue from clone). If recurrence shows up at curmudgeon, a follow-up directive can extend. Same logic for analyst / analyst-baby — held back pending evidence.

what_if_integrity_is_invoked_outside_a_c.objection: If a future operator-driven invocation runs integrity from outside a clone (e.g., directly in FUSE), the PROLOGUE rule is unenforceable.
what_if_integrity_is_invoked_outside_a_c.response: True. The PROLOGUE elevates the discipline to a rule but the runtime enforcement remains procedural (the agent must follow it). Three layers of defense converge: (a) integrity's own SKILL.md / scheduled-task wiring sets up a clone (existing); (b) the prompt's Section 9 Build Reproducibility section already uses /tmp/dome-integrity-clone; (c) the new PROLOGUEs in 7a.5 and 7h make the read+write path explicit. A runtime-enforcement gate (e.g., a pre-write check that exits if the destination is under /sessions/*/mnt) is a separate PROP if the procedural approach proves insufficient.
